text:
### Observed differences

- The repetitive fragment A36–A37 is traversed much less in the later window: earlier, A37 appeared in about 60 in 100 traces (about 1.1 occurrences per trace, with repeats in about 31 in 100 of the traces containing it) and A36 in about 31 in 100; in the later window A37 appears in about 48 in 100 traces (about 0.8 occurrences per trace, repeats in about 21 in 100) and A36 in about 22 in 100. [OCC033, OCC034]
- The entry into this fragment moved at its branch point A16, which itself still occurs in every trace at a nearly unchanged level (about 1.6 occurrences per trace in both windows): after A16, continuations into A37 fell from about 35 to 29 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, while continuations into A17 rose from about 11 to 15 and into A18 from about 14 to 18 in 100; accordingly A17 now appears in 24 vs 18 in 100 traces and A18 in 29 vs 23 in 100, and both routes still lead on to A38. [DIR016, OCC016, OCC017, OCC018, DIR017, DIR018]
- Visits to A37 also end sooner: A37 returns to A36 in about 40 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (was 48) and continues to A38 in about 60 in 100 (was 52), while A36 still returns to A37 almost always (95–99 in 100). [DIR037, DIR036]
- The loop around A39–A42 repeats more often: A39, present in every trace, averages about 1.7 occurrences per trace (was 1.5) and repeats within about 42 vs 31 in 100 traces; A40 appears in 64 vs 60 in 100 traces; after A40, returns to A39 rose from 33 to 40 in 100 while exits to A43 fell from 64 to 57, and after A42 the return share rose from 34 to 38 while the exit share fell from 65 to 60. [OCC035, OCC036, OCC037, OCC038, DIR040, DIR042]
- Within the A21–A24 cluster, traffic shifted from A23 to A24 while A21 and A22 stayed stable: A23 appears in 49 vs 55 in 100 traces and A24 in 52 vs 45; after A21, continuations into A23 fell from 32 to 22 in 100 and into A24 rose from 17 to 26 in 100, and visits to A24 now exit to A30 more often (48 vs 39 in 100). [OCC022, OCC023, DIR021, DIR024]
- After A30, the branch through A34/A35 is taken somewhat more often than the one through A32/A33: A34 and A35 each appear in about 52 vs 47 in 100 traces, A32 and A33 each in about 49 vs 54. [OCC029, OCC030, OCC031, OCC032, DIR030]
- Smaller, weakly supported movements: A08 appears in 14 vs 19 of 200 traces and A10 in 22 vs 16; routing shares around A01/A05/A07/A09/A14 wobble in inconsistent directions (after A05, A14 rises to 36 vs 27 in 100, but after A07 it falls to 29 vs 37) with unchanged participation; A15/A16 repeats are marginally lower; and routing profiles after rarely observed activities such as A02 and A44 rest on only about 1–14 observed transitions and cannot be interpreted. [OCC008, OCC010, DIR005, DIR007, OCC015, OCC016, DIR002, DIR044]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, traces bypass the repetitive A36–A37 fragment to a greater extent: fewer continuations from A16 enter A37 (about 29 vs 35 in 100) because the branch via A17 and A18 is taken more often, and a visit to A37 returns to A36 less often (about 40 vs 48 in 100), exiting sooner to A38; as a result A37 and A36 participate in fewer traces (about 48 vs 60 and 22 vs 31 in 100) and repeat less, while A17 (24 vs 18) and A18 (29 vs 23) participate in more traces. The reading is direct and consistent across the entry routing at A16, the per-visit routing of A37, and the participation of all activities involved; the participation drops for A37 and A36 exceed about 97–98 in 100 random re-splits, the shift at A37 about 88 in 100 and the branch shift at A16 about 79 in 100, and the routing shares rest on roughly 95–333 observed transitions. [OCC033, OCC034, OCC017, OCC018, DIR016, DIR036, DIR037]

Limitations: the two windows are finite samples, and the evidence cannot show whether the entry shift at A16 and the earlier exit at A37 are one coordinated difference or two independent routing adjustments, nor fully exclude sampling variation for the smaller share movements. A competing explanation for the growth of A17/A18 — additional entries from elsewhere in the process — is not supported, since A16 is their only substantial observed feeder in both windows. [DIR016, DIR037, DIR005]

Other differences:
- The A39–A42 loop repeats more often per trace, with more returns to A39 and fewer exits to A43; this is a repetition change in its own right, in a region downstream of the main hypothesis. [OCC035, OCC036, OCC037, OCC038, DIR040, DIR042]
- Traffic within the A21–A24 cluster shifted from A23 to A24, with A24 visits exiting to A30 more often. [OCC022, OCC023, DIR021, DIR024]
- The branch after A30 shifted toward A34/A35 and away from A32/A33; the direct routing item after A30 is weak (larger than only about 24 in 100 random re-splits), so this rests mainly on the occurrence shifts. [OCC029, OCC030, OCC031, OCC032, DIR030]
- Minor movements (A08 and A10 participation, routing wobbles around A01/A05/A07/A09/A14, marginally fewer A15/A16 repeats) are consistent with sampling noise. [OCC008, OCC010, DIR005, DIR007, OCC015, OCC016]
